result.topic_en: Euler finishes examples of curves through given points that turn out to be the sine and tangent curves. He notes that the integral Δ is expressible by angles in Problem 4 but not in Problem 3, and he begins Problem 5 on an interpolating curve with the abscissae nθ, (1±n)θ, (2±n)θ and alternating pairs of applicates ±f.
result.transcription:
202
Haec ergo curua denuo est linea sinuum; ac si sumatur $\theta = 2\pi$, vt sit $f = \sin. 2n\pi$, erit applicata $y = \sin. x$.

Corollarium 1.
§. 49. Si sumatur $\theta = \pi$ et $f = \tang. n\theta = \tang. n\pi$, puncta data erunt in linea tangentium; neque tamen ipsa curua inuenta erit linea tangentium: sed eius natura hac exprimetur aequatione:
$y = \frac{\tang. n\pi\,\sin. 2x}{\sin. 2n\pi} = \frac{\sin. 2x}{2\cos. n\pi^2} = \frac{\sin. 2x}{1+\cos. 2n\pi}$
eritque hic $y = \tang. x$, quoties fuerit $x = \pm(i \pm n)\pi$.

Corollarium 2.
§. 50. Si in solutione prioris exempli, quo erat $p = f$, $q = f$, $r = -f$, $s = -f$, $t = f$, $u = f$, statim loco $\Delta$ valorem inuentum posuissemus, prodiisset haec aequatio: $y = \frac{f\,\sin. \omega\pi}{\sin. n\pi}$. Vnde perspicuum fuisset, sumto $\theta = \pi$ et $f = \sin. n\pi$, curuam illam ipsam fore lineam sinuum.

Scholion.
§. 51. Omnino notari meretur, quod in problemate 4, vbi abscissae datae progressionem arithmeticam interruptam constituunt, valor quantitatis $\Delta$ absolute per angulos exhiberi potuerit, cum tamen in problemate 3, vbi abscissae datae veram progressionem arithmeticam constituebant, formula integralis $\Delta$ in genere neutiquam per angulos exprimi queat. Cum enim ibi esset
$\Delta = \int z^{n-\omega-1}\,dz\,(1-z)^{n-\omega-1}$,
haec formula, posito $n - \omega = \frac{\nu}{\lambda}$ et $z = v^{\lambda}$, abit in
$\Delta =$

203
$\Delta = \lambda\int \frac{v^{\nu-1}\,dv}{\sqrt[\lambda]{(1-v^{\lambda})^{\lambda-\nu}}}$, seu $\Delta = \lambda\left(\frac{\nu}{\lambda}\right)$,
quae formula quadraturas maxime transcendentes implicare potest. Ac si in illo problemate statuantur applicatae datae $p = f$, $q = -f$, $r = f$, $s = -f$, $t = f$, $u = -f$, etc. et $n = \frac{1}{2}$, aequatio pro curua per ista puncta transeunte erit:
$\frac{\Delta y}{2(1+2\omega)\omega f} = \frac{4}{1-4\omega\omega} + \frac{4}{9-4\omega\omega} + \frac{4}{25-4\omega\omega} + \text{etc.}$
seu $\frac{\Delta y}{2f\omega(1+2\omega)} = \frac{\pi}{2\omega}\tang. \omega\pi$, ita vt sit $y = \frac{\pi f(1+2\omega)\tang. \omega\pi}{\Delta}$,
vnde, etiamsi sumatur $\theta = \pi$ et $f = \sin. n\theta = \sin. \frac{1}{2}\pi = 1$, manifesto non sequitur fore $y = \sin. \theta\omega = \sin. \omega\pi$. Cum priori exemplo iam certum sit esse $y = \frac{f\,\sin. \omega\pi}{\sin. n\pi}$, eundem [?] casum ex problemate primo ita euoluamus, vt valores singulorum coefficientium A, B, C, D, etc. inuestigemus.

Problema 5.
§. 52. Aequationem generalem supra Problem. 1. constituram [?] ita determinare, vt respondeant his abscissis: $x = n\theta$, $(1-n)\theta$, $(1+n)\theta$, $(2-n)\theta$, $(2+n)\theta$, etc.
hae applicatae: $y = f$, $+f$, $-f$, $-f$, $+f$, $+f$, etc.

Solutio.
Statuatur vt ante $x = \theta\omega$, et consideretur aequatio quaesita sub hac forma:
$y = A\omega + B\omega(\omega\omega - nn) + C\omega(\omega\omega - nn)(\omega\omega - (1-n)^2)$
$+ D\omega(\omega\omega - nn)(\omega\omega - (1-n)^2)(\omega\omega - (1+n)^2)$
$+ E\omega(\omega\omega - nn)(\omega\omega - (1-n)^2)(\omega\omega - (1+n)^2)(\omega\omega - (2-n)^2)$
etc.
C c 2 vnde

items.quote: neque tamen ipsa curua inuenta erit linea tangentium: sed eius natura hac exprimetur aequatione
items.english: Yet the curve found will not itself be the tangent curve; instead its nature is expressed by this equation.

items.quote: Vnde perspicuum fuisset, sumto $\theta = \pi$ et $f = \sin. n\pi$, curuam illam ipsam fore lineam sinuum.
items.english: Hence it would have been clear that, taking θ = π and f = sin nπ, that curve is itself the sine curve.

items.quote: formula integralis $\Delta$ in genere neutiquam per angulos exprimi queat
items.english: In Problem 3, where the given abscissae formed a true arithmetic progression, the integral formula Δ can in general by no means be expressed through angles.
Even if θ = π and f = sin ½π = 1 are taken, it clearly does not follow that y = sin θω = sin ωπ.

items.quote: eundem [?] casum ex problemate primo ita euoluamus, vt valores singulorum coefficientium A, B, C, D, etc. inuestigemus.
items.english: Let us work out the same case from the first problem, so as to investigate the values of the individual coefficients A, B, C, D, etc.

items.quote:
Aequationem generalem supra Problem. 1. constituram [?] ita determinare, vt respondeant his abscissis: $x = n\theta$, $(1-n)\theta$, $(1+n)\theta$, $(2-n)\theta$, $(2+n)\theta$, etc.
hae applicatae: $y = f$, $+f$, $-f$, $-f$, $+f$, $+f$, etc.
items.english: To determine the general equation set up above in Problem 1 so that to the abscissae x = nθ, (1−n)θ, (1+n)θ, (2−n)θ, (2+n)θ, etc. correspond the applicates y = f, +f, −f, −f, +f, +f, etc.
